Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Greenville-Spartanburg SC
635 AM EST Sun Nov 22 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Likelihood of dense fog early Monday morning has increased. 

Rain chances continue to trend up for the middle of the week.

Aviation discussion was updated to reflect the 12Z TAFs.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. Showers will continue through Sunday across much of the area,
dense fog possible Monday morning.
2. Warm Monday and then cooler from Tuesday onward with increasing
precipitation chances by midweek.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Key message 1: Showers will continue through Sunday across much of the 
area, dense fog possible Monday morning.

The synoptic pattern remains largely progressive across the CONUS 
with a deep longwave trough situated over the Great Plains. Ahead of 
this feature, a weak wave was noted over the southeast with a 
surface reflection along the coast as a pair of surface lows lifts 
northeast. Surface high pressure that fostered the development of a 
Cold Air Damming wedge across the area has shifted offshore with 
support for the CAD gradually waning as it shifts to diabatically 
enhanced in-situ. Persistent, but relatively weak, east/southeast 
low-level flow continues to support isentropic ascent atop the CAD 
wedge with a scattering of light showers noted on area radars. This 
will continue overnight and through much of the day on Sunday. By 
Sunday evening, the CAD demise will be underway as surface high 
pressure moves well offshore and the coastal low lifts towards New 
England ahead of an advancing cold front over the Mississippi 
Valley. This will allow for wedge erosion with isentropic ascent 
also shutting off. Residual boundary layer moisture may support the 
development of a dense fog event Monday morning.


Key message 2: Warm Monday and then cooler from Tuesday onward with 
increasing precipitation chances by midweek.

Heading into the start of the holiday week, a potent northern stream 
trough will be swinging across the Great Lakes region with a surface 
cold front draped through the Ohio Valley into central Tennessee. 
Compressional warming ahead of the boundary in concert with the 
demise of the weekend CAD wedge will result in a noticeably warm day 
with high temperatures in the low 60s to low 70s. A few readings 
nearing the mid 70s will be possible across the southern Upstate. 
This will be short lived, however, as the frontal boundary pushes 
across the area Monday night into Tuesday morning. This will be a 
dry frontal passage outside of the potential for a few mountain 
showers that will mainly be confined to the Tennessee border. A 
sprawling surface high settles across the Midwest on Tuesday and 
subsequently translates across the Great Lakes and into the Mid-
Atlantic/New England Tuesday night into Wednesday. This will set the 
stage for another CAD event with a classic surface pressure pattern 
and dry/cool northeast winds. This will usher in a cooler and more 
seasonable airmass through the remainder of the week.

The other focus will be on an active southern stream that looks to 
bring a well defined storm system across the area Wednesday into 
Thursday. Guidance progs a notable sub-tropical jet extending across 
northern Mexico while several pieces of energy eject out of the 
Rockies. A southern stream wave is forecast to slide across the 
Southern Plains while a northern stream trough drops across the 
Northern Plains into the Midwest. Guidance continues to differ with 
how these features may interact, but the bottom line and overall 
consensus amongst ensemble means is that at a minimum the southern 
stream trough will take on a negative tilt over the Deep South and 
help to instigate surface cyclogenesis along a coastal baroclinic 
zone. The surface low would likely deepen as it lifts along the 
Carolina coast with low-level mass response strengthening a stout 
low-level jet with copious onshore flow. As such, confidence 
continues to increase the widespread rain chances will return across 
the area Wednesday into Thursday. As of now, this would appear to 
just be a beneficial rain with no hazards expected, but this is 
subject to change as model guidance comes into better agreement with 
respect to the evolution of the upper-level features.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
At KCLT and elsewhere: Another restriction filled TAF period for the 
12Z update. Intermittent gusts linger across the SC Upstate 
terminals this morning but should diminish by late morning. Cigs are 
mainly MVFR with some pockets of IFR and vsbys are mainly VFR with 
some pockets of MVFR as of 1130Z. -RA will linger over the terminals 
through at least the late morning hours. 06Z guidance shows -RA 
tapering off faster compared to the 00Z guidance so went with TEMPOs 
12-16Z across the terminals. Only have a PROB30 at KCLT from 16-19Z 
as -RA could linger a bit longer at this terminal. Vsbys should drop 
a bit lower after daybreak but are not expected to fall below MVFR 
levels. Cigs should lift back to VFR briefly this afternoon/early 
evening. Cigs will gradually lower after daybreak as well, becoming 
IFR. Guidance is now showing the potential for cigs to briefly lift 
to MVFR levels late this afternoon into late this evening as well as 
cloud cover gradually becoming SCT to BKN. Wind speeds will 
gradually decrease throughout today, with calm to light and VRB 
winds developing this evening into tonight. SCT cloud cover will 
gradually lower to IFR/LIFR levels overnight. Decreasing cloud 
cover, light winds, and lingering low-level moisture should lead to 
widespread patchy to dense fog tonight into daybreak Monday, with 
IFR to LIFR vsby restrictions possible.

Outlook: Drier conditions linger through Tuesday before widespread 
rain chances and possible restrictions return midweek.
